judge_panel.reason: The paper explicitly notes in Section 2.3 that 'there is no significant overdensity that includes all 4 QGs' in two alternative catalogs, and the overdensity significance relies on photometric-redshift slices with boundary corrections, without providing mock catalogs, randomized controls, or false-positive rates to assess the probability of such structures arising by chance.

The paper’s support for the structures is limited to modest overdensity estimates—“revealing a marginally significant overdensity (δ ∼ 1.6)” and “SXDS-27434 is also located within the large-scale overdensity (δ ∼ 1.8)”—and Sec. 2.3 further notes that “there is no significant overdensity that includes all 4 QGs” in other catalogs. Nowhere does the paper present mock-catalog tests, randomized controls, or false-positive-rate estimates to quantify robustness against projection effects.

The paper acknowledges that "there is no significant overdensity that includes all 4 QGs" when using certain catalogs, but relies on a simple kernel density estimation without providing mock catalogs or false-positive rates to definitively rule out projection effects.

The paper does make a control comparison—“We randomly drew subsets of 7 galaxies from the 14 field QGs” and notes that “the stellar mass distribution of field QGs is also consistent with the QGs in the overdensities”—but it also concedes that “Although limited by sample statistics, this hints at similar SFHs of the member QGs.” The comparison is therefore not absent, yet the paper does not explicitly show matching in several other dimensions raised by the flag (e.g. S/N, spectral setup/coverage, selection function).

The paper performs its comparison by stating, "We randomly drew subsets of 7 galaxies from the 14 field QGs," but does not explicitly match the control sample on key observational properties like individual redshift, S/N, or spectral coverage.

judge_panel.reason: The paper's Conclusion states 'merger-induced AGN deplete the molecular gas surrounding of galaxies, which causes synchronous quenching,' but Section 4.2 finds only one clear broad-line/X-ray AGN, Section 5.2 relies on a single TNG300 analog, and Section 5.3 acknowledges molecular gas constraints only for part of the COSMOS system, while elsewhere noting that 'merger events are not strictly necessary to reproduce massive galaxies in the early Universe.'

The direct evidence is limited: in Sec. 4.2, “DD-78 is located in the AGN region, and DD-126 and DD-79 have a possibility of being classified as AGNs (or composite spectra),” and Sec. 5.2 admits “this merger-driven scenario is only one of the possible interpretations.” Yet the Conclusion states that “merger-induced AGN deplete the molecular gas surrounding of galaxies, which causes synchronous quenching of the QGs,” which is stronger than what the observations directly demonstrate.

The conclusion asserts that "merger-induced AGN deplete the molecular gas... which causes synchronous quenching," but the text makes clear this causal chain is strongly inferred from an "Illustris TNG300 simulation" analog rather than directly observed across all members.
